source.title: On the Effect of the Activation Function on the Distribution of Hidden Nodes in a Deep Network

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes random-initialization signal lengths across layers, a component of V4, using a theoretical convergence analysis and simulations. It does not measure training speed or trainable depth.
record.gate_note: The theorem and counterexamples report length-distribution results. The simulations verify the Cauchy-distribution and dependence findings; these are not training outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study proves results about hidden-variable distributions at random initialization. It does not measure training speed, trainable depth, gradient propagation or optimization outcomes. Convergence to a length map does not establish that signals remain stable across depth or that initialization improves training, so it does not test V4 or another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: permissible activations yield convergence of the length process to the length map as width grows at fixed depth; non-permissible activations can violate this behavior, and finite-width ReLU and Heaviside networks can have dependent second-layer preactivations. These conclusions do not establish training benefits.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies layerwise activation-length distributions under random Gaussian initialization; it does not compare activation-matched initializations or measure training speed or trainable depth.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation-function assumptions change whether the length map is defined and whether the stated convergence result applies; the paper also reports dependence for ReLU and Heaviside.

fits_no_version.finding: For permissible activations, layerwise mean squared preactivation lengths converge in probability to a deterministic recursion as width increases at fixed depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide Gaussian-initialized fully connected networks have concentrating layerwise preactivation lengths under the stated activation assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: With reciprocal activation and zero biases, second-layer preactivations have Cauchy(0, √N) distributions; simulations qualitatively match this distribution and illustrate within-layer dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reciprocal activation can produce heavy-tailed, dependent preactivations without a finite wide-network distributional limit.

fits_no_version.finding: Second-layer preactivations are dependent for finite-width ReLU and Heaviside networks; the dependence established by the proof diminishes with width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-width Gaussian-initialized networks need not have independent preactivations within a layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 11 shows that exp(αx²) activations can make the length recursion undefined for suitable initialization variances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation growth conditions restrict when a finite length recursion exists at random initialization.

record.problems: The paper provides no training outcomes, so it cannot establish training speed or trainable depth. The experiments report qualitative histogram comparisons without numerical fit or dependence statistics. The independence result is proved for ReLU and Heaviside, but the accompanying simulations use φ(z)=1/z.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V4 verdicts. Counterexamples to unrestricted length-map or independence assumptions do not challenge the training claims in V4. Proposition 11 is an additional related finding, but no omitted result bears directly on a listed version.

rows.subject: fully connected width-N network with permissible activation φ
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 2 analyzes convergence of the layerwise mean squared preactivation lengths to the recursively defined length map as width grows.
rows.measure: Convergence in probability of q0,...,qD to q̃0,...,q̃D.
rows.value: For any ε, δ > 0, for sufficiently large N, with probability 1 − δ, |qℓ − q̃ℓ| ≤ ε for all ℓ ∈ {0,...,D}.
rows.uncertainty: Probability bound 1 − δ; ε and δ are arbitrary positive values.
rows.note: The result concerns signal-length behavior at random initialization, not learning or training speed.
rows.check: Theorem 2 establishes concentration around a length recursion for any fixed depth as width increases. It does not establish preservation of signal scale across depth or improved training.

rows.subject: fully connected width-N network with φ(y)=1/y for y≠0 and φ(0)=0
rows.operation_detail: Proposition 9 analyzes the second-layer preactivation distribution as width grows.
rows.value: For finite N, h2,1 has distribution Cauchy(0, √N); it diverges as N goes to infinity.
rows.note: A counterexample to convergence for this non-permissible activation; the result is about initial signal lengths, not training.
rows.check: The reciprocal-activation counterexample concerns initial preactivation distributions, not a reversal of V4. Divergence means no limiting probability distribution on the reals as width grows; no training outcome is measured.

rows.subject: fully connected width-N network with ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 10 measures dependence between second-layer preactivations.
rows.value: The second-layer preactivations are not independent; the paper says the degree of dependence approaches 0 as N gets large.
rows.note: This dependence result does not measure the training-speed or trainable-depth outcomes in V4.
rows.check: Dependence among initial preactivations does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: fully connected width-N network with Heaviside activation
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 10 measures dependence between second-layer preactivations.
rows.value: The second-layer preactivations are not independent.
rows.note: This dependence result does not measure the training-speed or trainable-depth outcomes in V4.
rows.check: Dependence among initial preactivations does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: fully connected width-N network with φ(z)=1/z
rows.operation_detail: The experiment compares histograms of second-layer activations across random initializations with Cauchy and fitted Gaussian distributions.
rows.measure: Fit of the second-layer activation distribution to Cauchy versus Gaussian.
rows.baseline: Gaussian with σ estimated from the data
rows.value: The Cauchy(0, √N) distribution fits the data well.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative fit, not numerical fit statistics.
rows.check: The plotted h[2,:] values are preactivations. Their qualitative fit to a Cauchy distribution is not an optimization outcome; observed is not an appropriate state against the listed versions.

rows.subject: fully connected width-1000 network with φ(z)=1/z
rows.operation_detail: The experiment plots second-layer preactivation histograms for separate random weight initializations.
rows.measure: Dependence among second-layer activations across units.
rows.value: The plots reveal dependence among activations; the text describes coordinated large values when some first-layer values have unusually small magnitude.
rows.note: No numerical dependence measure is reported.
rows.check: The plotted h[2,:] values are preactivations. Coordinated magnitudes illustrate dependence at initialization without measuring any listed version.
